lead.zh-Hans: 这朵花不用浇水，我的铅笔需要削。
lead.en: The flower needed no watering. My pencil needed sharpening.

text.zh-Hans: 联合国广场的金属花让我在布宜诺斯艾利斯停住。铝和不锈钢做成花的样子，我却把纸上的花瓣画得像一把勺子。旅人说可以先看边缘，再补中间。我准备给它另留一张纸，免得这把勺子占满整封家信。
text.en: Floralis Genérica stopped me in Buenos Aires. The aluminium and steel flower became something like a spoon in my drawing. A traveler suggested following the edges before filling the middle. I will give it another sheet, so the spoon does not occupy this entire letter home.
Talk about that drawn spoon
Draw along the petal edges

lead.zh-Hans: 口袋里多了一张纸，没有多一片叶。
lead.en: One more sheet in my pocket, no extra leaves.

text.zh-Hans: 植物园里的棕榈和仙人掌，我都只用眼睛看。想记下来时，就在布宜诺斯艾利斯的便纸上分开画两种轮廓。出园摸口袋，只有自己带来的纸和笔。这样轻轻的，也能把一路的认真寄给你。
text.en: I looked at palms and cacti in Buenos Aires Botanical Garden, drawing separate outlines on my own paper. At the exit, my pockets held only the pencil and stationery I had brought. A light load, but enough to send home a little of the attention I paid.
Describe the different outlines
Look at each outline separately

lead.zh-Hans: 半月形的午饭，不需要写邮编。
lead.en: My crescent-shaped lunch needed no postcode.

text.zh-Hans: 吃布宜诺斯艾利斯的烤馅饼，我在菜单上画半月形，给肉馅那份做个小记号。笔停下时，差点顺手写上家里的地址。大概是太习惯寄信了。我把地址留给信封，菜单只写菜名，午饭就不会走错地方。
text.en: For a baked meat empanada in Buenos Aires, I drew a crescent and marked the filling on my menu. My hand almost added your address. Too much letter-writing, perhaps. I saved the address for the envelope; lunch needs its name rather than postal instructions.
Read lunch its own name
Find the filling’s small marker

lead.zh-Hans: 手指擦干净，才轮到写“你好”。

text.zh-Hans: 吉拿棒外面裹着糖，我在布宜诺斯艾利斯吃完后仔细擦手，才翻开写给你的纸。想起刚才那一口，在小菜单上加了细细的点。点画得太密，又像一封全是省略号的信。还好这封真的信，我有话要说。
text.en: After sugar-coated churros in Buenos Aires, I cleaned my fingers before opening your letter paper. Dots on the little menu recalled the coating. I made so many that the sketch resembled a letter made entirely of ellipses. Fortunately, this actual letter has something to say.
Say what comes after those dots
Notice the spacing of the dots

lead.zh-Hans: 我让菜单替我先把话说完整。
lead.en: I let the menus finish the sentence first.

text.zh-Hans: 说到布宜诺斯艾利斯的馅饼和吉拿棒，我总想先讲形状，忘了讲味道。旅人把两张小菜单递回来，叫我各添一句自己的感受。我写“这份咸的”“那份甜的”，然后笑了。旅途报告还很短，但已经肯把自己的那一口算进去。
text.en: When talking about empanadas and churros in Buenos Aires, I kept describing shapes and forgetting taste. A traveler handed back the menus: add your own impression to each. “This one savoury; that one sweet,” I wrote. A short report, but at least my own meal has entered it.
Add your own impression
Find the two small notes

lead.zh-Hans: 两张干净纸，分住两个小格。
lead.en: Two clean sheets found separate little spaces.

text.zh-Hans: 整理布宜诺斯艾利斯的菜单，我把馅饼纸和吉拿棒纸折成一样宽。前者的半月线条，后者的糖点，不用打开也能从纸边认出来。我做了两个纸套分着放。信写完再收好，别让菜单抢先被我封进回家的信里。
text.en: I folded my Buenos Aires empanada and churro menus to the same width. A crescent edge and a few sugar dots still told them apart. I made two paper sleeves. They will wait until this letter is sealed; otherwise a menu may accidentally become the message home.
Choose words for the sleeves
Identify each menu at its edge

lead.en: Following “{reply},” I began with the outside.

text.zh-Hans: 我给金属花换了张纸，按你说的沿花瓣边缘慢慢画。中间暂时空着，先把每道线接好。那把误画出来的勺子终于收工了。我把新轮廓折成卡寄给你，布宜诺斯艾利斯这朵花在纸上也有了自己的位置。
text.en: On fresh paper, I followed the edges of Floralis Genérica’s petals as you suggested, leaving the middle open. The accidental spoon has retired. I folded the new outline into a card for you. This Buenos Aires flower now has a place of its own on my paper.
Name the new outline
Look at the joined edges

lead.zh-Hans: 金属花前，我和旅人一起围住了杯盖。
lead.en: A bottle cap sent two visitors shuffling beside the metal flower.

text.zh-Hans: 杯盖从我脚边滚出去，停在一位旅人的鞋后。这趟重来，我刚在联合国广场认出那朵金属花，放心拧开水壶，手就滑了一下。对方以为碰到了小虫，抬脚躲开，杯盖又往旁边跑。我俩赶紧用鞋围出一个圈，才把它截住。重新盖好壶，我还得擦擦袖口，那里印着一个湿漉漉的小圆圈。
text.en: My bottle cap rolled behind another visitor’s shoe. I had just recognised Floralis Genérica on my return to Buenos Aires and stopped in Plaza de las Naciones Unidas for a drink. Then my fingers slipped. The visitor felt something, lifted a foot as though avoiding an insect, and sent the cap rolling again. We shuffled our shoes into a little enclosure and caught it between us. The bottle was closed at last, but my cuff still wore a small wet ring.

text.zh-Hans: 讲讲两个人怎么截住杯盖
text.en: Tell how two visitors managed to catch the cap
Look at the wet ring on the cuff
